NoteTexAccessor::args¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::args(std::string_view cmd) const

Select One Command’s Required Arguments¶

args() extracts the first required braced argument from every invocation of one named TeX control word. It is useful when the command name is known but no dedicated semantic extractor exists: custom metadata commands, project-local macros, and ordinary commands such as caption can all be queried through the same operation. Pass either "caption" or R"(\caption)"; the optional leading backslash identifies the same control word.

The scanner respects control-word boundaries. Asking for caption does not match captioned, and a doubled backslash does not begin a command. Whitespace between the command and its arguments is permitted. One balanced optional argument is skipped, then the first balanced {...} group is returned without its outer braces. Nested braces and escaped braces remain in the payload. Malformed calls, calls without a required group, and incomplete optional groups contribute no token.

Tokens remain in source order and duplicates are retained. The result is a closed TokenBatch: tokens() is flat Text storage, while offsets() maps each logical receiver cell to its half-open token range. Receiver rank does not change that ragged representation. The receiver is not modified.

cmd must be a non-empty TeX control-word name made of letters or @, with an optional final *; invalid names throw pluss::Error. Undefined input yields undefined tokens and offsets [0]. Non-text Notes are rejected. Scanning is linear in input bytes plus copied payload bytes.

Example 1: Optional And Nested Groups¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(\caption[Short]{A {nested} title} \caption{Second})",
        R"(\captioned{not a caption} \\caption{escaped})",
        R"(\caption {Third})", R"(\caption[broken{ignored})"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().args("caption");
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A {nested} title", "Second", "Third"]

Example 2: Recover The Four Input Cells¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\nshape=[" << source.sizes()[0] << ", "
          << source.sizes()[1] << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 3, 3]
shape=[2, 2]

The second and fourth cells own empty ranges; no placeholder token is created.

Example 3: Name Validation And Dtype Failure¶

try { (void)source.tex().args(""); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "args(empty): rejected\n"; }
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().args("caption");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "command arguments Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

args(empty): rejected
command arguments Int64: rejected
